subject: EXIT statement
notes: kb/Work PB403. The rule names a SET, and the binder tested a SCALAR. 14.2.2 SR10 enumerates the five source elements that may carry a Format-1/2 procedure division - 'a function definition, a function prototype definition, a method definition, a program definition, or a program prototype definition' - so four of them are not a program's; BindExit's SR7 arm tested the single predicate host.InMethod and therefore refused exactly ONE of the four. Measured before the fix on d80cb676: a FUNCTION definition ending in EXIT PROGRAM compiled with only the COBOL0903 archaic warning and RAN, and the generated function class carried the PROGRAM-activation machinery (a private __asCalled field plus a throw new ProgramReturn()), so program-shaped emission leaked into a function definition. A function PROTOTYPE definition did the same (probe sr7-proto.cob) - the prototype arm is REACHABLE, not vacuous: 10.1's general format admits a procedure division in a prototype and this compiler binds it. Now the arm asks ctx.Enclosing.InProgramProcedureDivision, the one bind-position probe whose SourceElementKind is SR10's enumeration, and names the offending element in the message. READING RECORDED (design D14): a PROGRAM PROTOTYPE definition IS admitted - the noun in both of SR10's program items is 'program', and the alternative reading would reject source the standard nowhere forbids; a function prototype is refused, because the noun there is 'function'. That reading is currently UNEXERCISED and is recorded as such rather than claimed: the grammar's programIdAttribute admits only COMMON / INITIAL / RECURSIVE / GLOBAL, so 11.10.2's Format-2 PROGRAM-ID ... IS PROTOTYPE does not parse at all (COBOL0901 on the reserved word) and BinderDriver.MakeUnit derives IsPrototype from the FUNCTION-ID paragraph alone - a separate, filed defect. ExitPlacementContextDriftTests pins that parse refusal, so landing the grammar arm turns the fact RED and forces SR7's program-prototype verdict to be pinned for real. The three arms the language CAN express today - function definition, function prototype definition, method definition - are each covered. The pre-existing test covered only the METHOD arm, which is why the row read PARTIAL and a green gate never saw the other two. retired-witness: conformance-test:ExitPlacementContextDriftTests.ProgramPrototypeDefinition_IsNotYetWritable_SoSr7sPrototypeArmIsUnexercised (kb/Work PB894 made the program prototype writable; the fact pinned the COBOL0901 parse refusal and was replaced by the real SR7 program-prototype verdict (admitted by SR7, refused by 10.6.2 SR4 f))
